newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technical rally.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas ends up on technical rally.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures ended higher across the board Friday in a moderate session, with a steady weekend cash market and some technical buying and short covering boosting the complex, sources said.
July jumped 6.9 cents to close at $2.149 per million British thermal units. August settled 6.1 cent higher at $2.167. Other months ended up by 1.5 to 5.1 cents.

"There was a lot of short covering ahead of the weekend due to the possibility of warmer temperatures over a major portion of the country next week, but I think we'll be bumping our heads at anything over $2.20," said one Texas trader.
He was referring to one private forecaster expecting above-normal temperatures across the southern half of the nation by midweek next week.

But traders noted extended forecasts varied, with the National Weather Service expecting warm temperatures in the western half of the U.S. and Florida, while the Midwest and East should range from normal to slightly below.

Chart traders turned more positive with Friday's strong close, which confirmed a short-term reversal on Thursday, but many remained skeptical about further upside unless the heat next week is enough to rally the cash.

"Cash is stable, but there's not a whole lot out there to get it going (much higher). It may be a little early for a major selloff, but if we don't get sustained heat soon, I think you'll see it dump," said one East Coast trader.
July support was still pegged at $2.055, with better buying expected in front of $2. Resistance was now seen at $2.21, $2.25 and then at the recent highs in the $2.37 area.

In the cash Friday, Louisiana Gulf Coast gas was talked little changed in the low-teens. Midcon pipes were steady to down slightly in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate weekend gas was flat in the $2.35-2.40 range.
The NYMEX 12-month Henry Hub strip rallied 4.1 cents to $2.237. NYMEX said 42,767 contracts traded, up from Thursday's revised tally of 33,694.

On the KCBT, July finished 6.3 cents higher at $2.013, while deferreds ended up by five tp 6.5 cents. The East/West spread widened by 0.6 cent to 13.6 cents (NYMEX premium). KCBT said 180 lots traded, down from Thursday's total of 198.
